question: Poorly controlled diabetes mellitus impairs wound healing primarily by reducing collagen synthesis in the proliferative phase only, leaving the inflammatory and haemostatic phases unaffected.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. Diabetes affects wound healing across multiple phases — it impairs neutrophil chemotaxis and phagocytosis during the inflammatory phase, reduces growth factor production, impairs collagen synthesis and cross-linking, and causes ischaemia through microvascular disease.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Diabetes impairs multiple phases: hyperglycaemia impairs neutrophil function (inflammatory phase), reduces growth factor release, impairs collagen cross-linking, and causes microvascular disease that starves the wound of oxygen and nutrients.
